description: Registry of clause tags for docs that carry stable clause identifiers and normative language. Tags: 'check-exists' — a named, runnable check already guards the clause (check-ref points at it); 'checkable' — a mechanical check can guard the clause but is not built yet (check-ref names the intended check and any interim probe); 'judgment-only' — compliance is a per-change judgment no check can decide (justification says why). Clause identifiers are stable: never renumbered, and a retired identifier stays reserved (listed under 'retired'). A row that states a check-ref may also carry 'test-cases': the identifiers of the test cases pinning the clause, each of which the registry check resolves against the declarators of the anchor-bearing files that row's check-ref cites by path — the title a bare 'it'/'test' call states in a .js or .mjs file, or the name an 'fn' declares in a .rs one. The field is opt-in, and stating it is what puts those identifiers under the check.

scripts/check-capture-surface.js (npm run lint:capture-surface, a step in CI's lint job) diffs the recorder's document listener registrations both ways against the DOM events this clause enumerates, holding the receiver this clause states as part of that surface: an enumerated event registered on window instead is reported on both sides, as a listener on the wrong receiver and as an enumerated event the recorder no longer registers. It holds every chrome listener registration the extension's tracked production JavaScript makes — the population derived as git ls-files over packages/extension, filtered to the JavaScript modules (.js, .mjs, .cjs) the package tracks outside its packages/extension/tests tree, so a production directory the package grows enters the closure the day it lands — to the check's own admission list, keyed by file and API path with an exact occurrence count and a stated role per entry, or, where the service worker is the file that makes it, to the proxy table's event-source column; and diffs that column's worker events both ways against the service worker's registrations, each held to a single registration, with a DOM event named there held to this clause's enumeration. The proxy route is the worker's alone, and the refusal names the route the file it fires on can take: the doc or the admission list for the worker, the admission list for every other file. The DOM read runs over that same population: this clause enumerates the recorder's surface, so the recorder's document listeners are diffed against it both ways, and a document or window listener any other population file registers reds as capture no enumeration describes, with no admission route offered for one — the admission list admits chrome roles, which a listener on the page's own event stream is not. That population is itself held non-empty and required to carry both capture files, so a file list that stopped naming what it exists to hold reds rather than passing over what is left; a population file that registers nothing either enumeration describes contributes nothing, which is the ordinary case there; and the per-file registrations are held to state that same set of files, an entry naming a file outside the population and a population file carrying no entry each refused as machinery rather than diffed. What sits outside this closure's subject is drawn by receiver and registration root, never by which file a registration is in: a listener bound to an element, and an addListener chain rooted anywhere but chrome — a message port's onMessage among them — register on nothing either enumeration describes, so beyond the capture pair they are passed over in silence rather than refused with no route to green, while inside the pair each is refused where it stands. Read through the shared comment-safe tokenizer, so a commented-out registration is never counted, and refusing rather than skipping a computed event name wherever the registration is in scope, a listener receiver outside the modelled set in the capture pair, an unreadable enumeration item or table cell, and an empty parse. The recorder's registrations sit outside the mirrored capture block, so the one production copy is what is read; the block itself stays held by the parity test. Named residue: in the capture pair every shape outside the scan's model is refused rather than skipped — an event name that is not a lone quoted string literal (a concatenated, computed, template, or regular-expression name is refused, never read as its leading fragment), a receiver outside document and window, which is what a helper taking its target as a parameter looks like wherever that helper is defined, and an addListener chain not rooted at chrome; beyond the pair the receiver and the root draw that boundary instead, an unreadable event name on a document or window listener staying refused there because the registration is in scope and only its name unread. What is genuinely invisible is a registration site that lands outside the scanned population: a helper defined elsewhere and merely called here registers nothing these files show, and the extension's test tree is outside the population by the derivation's own filter, a listener a test registers on a page it drives being that test's fixture rather than a surface the extension ships. The tokenizer models template literals as a type of their own and tokenizes each interpolation's contents as the code they are, so a registration written inside an interpolation is read as one; how it reads a regular-expression literal, with the shapes where that reading and the grammar part, is stated at the tokenizer's own home, scripts/check-test-inventory.js, and those shapes reach this scan in both directions. The pattern a literal read as division puts into the stream is read as the code that text spells, so a registration written inside one is credited as a registration the file makes: an event the enumeration does not describe reds there, naming a registration no source wrote. Past an unmatched quote written in such a pattern the stream stays out of step to the end of that file, and a registration standing beyond such a quote, or inside what a division read as a literal takes out of the stream, at most the rest of its own line, is not seen: silently where nothing else names it, and loudly where the enumeration does, since the DOM leg diffs both ways and an unseen registration reds there as an enumerated event the recorder no longer registers — a mismatch red naming an event the recorder does register. Beyond that, the capture phase this clause also states is not read — the scan parses no listener options, so the phase claim stays review-held — and whether a handler still captures what its enumeration entry describes is review-held.

Each of those two reads takes a quoted string literal that its own end follows — the label's colon, and the punctuation that ends the equality's right-hand operand (a closing bracket, a statement or argument separator, a conditional's punctuation, or the first character of && or ||) — so a type built around a literal is refused by name rather than credited with its leading piece, and a template literal in either position is refused the same way. The sender side is read the same way, over the tracked JavaScript under packages/extension/sidepanel/ (git ls-files over that directory, recursive, filtered by extension): a send call whose first argument opens an object literal is read, that literal's top-level properties (brace-depth bounded, so a nested payload's own type is never read as the message's) scanned for a type key — bare or quoted, in any position, since property order carries no meaning — carrying a lone string literal, with the token after that literal required to be the property separator or the literal's closing brace, so a concatenation is refused instead of being credited with its leading piece; a send stating no such property is refused by name, and the diagnosis names what the scan found in its place rather than the key it wanted. The types those calls state are diffed both ways against the same panel-protocol enumeration, and the clause's own sender statement (the runtime doc's panel-sends-literally paragraph inside ERT-4) is the doctrine that leg holds — held present as it is read: this clause's own scope must carry that statement's existence claim exactly once, sought over that scope whitespace-flattened so the words are found whatever line the prose wraps on, with the absence refused (the leg cannot go on holding a rule the document has stopped making) and a second occurrence refused beside it wherever in the clause it stands, a paragraph of its own or the one the claim already sits in (an update would land on one copy and leave another standing). The two doc enumerations must be disjoint, every cell must be a lone backticked name, and empty parses, machinery failures (a population that names no file, one that has lost the service worker), and anchor failures (no dispatcher switch in the population, more than one, one standing outside the service worker, a switch with no readable body, a missing default: arm, a nested dispatcher) fail loudly. Named residue: equality guards are collected population-wide and deduplicated, while the forward capture-path diff is held to the service worker's own guards, so a guard on a documented type that survives only in another background module still reds there; where inside the worker its guards sit is review-held, this clause's ahead-of-the-switch mechanism being doctrine the scan does not verify (token order is not control flow); the dispatcher's location leg holds one direction only — it pins the file the found switch stands in to the check's own service-worker path constant, whose comment cites this document's Components table, so editing that table's row alone leaves the check reading its constant and the doc-side direction stays review-held; a dispatch route outside the tokenized shapes (a computed message type, a negated or reversed-operand type test, an equality test on another receiver) is invisible to the scan; the tokenizer models template literals as a type of their own, which is also what keeps a template out of the type key position, and tokenizes each interpolation's contents as the code they are, so a send written inside one is read as a send; how it reads a regular-expression literal, with the shapes where that reading and the grammar part, is stated at the tokenizer's own home, scripts/check-test-inventory.js, and those shapes cost this check in both directions: the pattern a literal read as division puts into the stream is read as the code that text spells, so a send written inside one is credited as a send the panel makes, and a type the enumeration does not state reds there, naming a send no source wrote; an unbalanced brace in such a pattern also moves the dispatcher's walk, which counts braces alone — a balanced pair moves it by nothing, and a bracket or a parenthesis costs it nothing at all — and what a moved bound costs is decided by where the literal stands: standing right after the switch's own opening brace it leaves every arm unread and the check reds vacuously, naming no type; and past an unmatched quote written in such a pattern the stream stays out of step to the end of that file, so a send site standing beyond such a quote, or inside what a division read as a literal takes out of the stream, at most the rest of its own line, is simply not seen. Every one of those readings is one the whole population can pay for: each background module is tokenized on its own, so a pattern in one of them can put a switch head or an equality hit into that file's stream that no source wrote, or take one out of it, moving the counted switch total, the file a switch is attributed to, and the guards collected — while the bound stays the file's own, an out-of-step stream reaching the end of that file and no further. scripts/check-adapter-surface.js (npm run lint:adapter-surface, a step in CI's lint job) reads the declared contract from packages/shared/views/adapter.js — the one JSDoc block declaring the PlatformAdapter typedef, each @property entry inside it stating its brace-delimited type and its member name on one line — and diffs it in both directions against the members each concrete adapter implements. WHICH files those are is derived from this clause's own naming rule rather than listed: the tracked files under packages/ named adapter-<platform>.js, outside the packages' test trees and with the contract file excluded as the one named path it is — today packages/extension/sidepanel/adapter-chrome.js and packages/desktop/src/adapter-tauri.js, and tomorrow whatever a new platform adds, with the surface key each leg runs under derived from the same name. A name sitting where an adapter sits whose platform token that rule cannot take, and two adapters claiming one token, are refused rather than left unread. The same derivation is diffed against this document's own enumeration of the seam, read as the files the adapter-seam section's links TARGET rather than as the basenames it prints, in both directions; and a derivation finding fewer than two adapters reds outright, since the direction over the members every adapter implements states nothing below two and a leg that quietly holds nothing is the failure this gate exists to refuse. Each adapter's members are read through the shared comment-safe tokenizer as the object literal that file's default export names: the single export default statement is resolved to the one binding of that name the file declares — a const, let, or var declaration, the grammar the scan accepts — that binding's initializer is read as an object literal or refused, and the members are read from the literal's own braces, brace-depth bounded — so a member of a second top-level literal in the same file never satisfies a declared member, which is the shape the desktop adapter's exported test-only literal sits in today. Within that literal a member is read where a property can start, as a name or a quoted name followed by a colon, by an argument list, or by the property's end, with async admitted before a method name and read as the member name itself where the property's shape is its own; every other property shape — an accessor, a computed key, a spread, a generator, anything else — is refused by name rather than skipped. What the walk classifies as a property is what that refusal covers: a comma standing where a property would start is the separator it is rather than a shape, so a doubled comma is read through rather than refused — text no valid JavaScript carries, and the lint gate reds it on its own.
